description:
FILED s449s (Opus, agent S of round 7), found probing #564 -- the same
statement handler, the branch NEXT TO the one #564 added.  PRE-EXISTING and
SILENT: no drop announcement, no `;; PARSE ERROR`, no census row.

REPRO (probed, perl 5.40.3):

    no strict 'refs';
    our $g = "OUT";
    my $n = "g";
    { local ${$n} = "IN"; print "in=${$n}\n"; }
    print "out=$g\n";

    perl: in=IN   out=OUT
    PCL : in=     out=OUT      <- the assignment is GONE

CAUSE, located: the `local` deref branch (`Pl/Parser.pm`, the arm testing
`Cast in [$@%]` followed by Block/Symbol) reads ONLY the target.  It emits
`(p-local-deref-scalar REF ...)` -- which saves and restores the slot and
takes NO init form -- and returns; the `= RHS` half of the run is never
looked at.  The localization is right and the assignment vanishes, so the
scope sees undef where perl sees the value.

All three sigils are the same shape: `local ${$n} = V`, `local @{$n} = (…)`,
`local %{$n} = (…)`, and the `$$x` / `@$x` / `%$x` spellings of each.

SHAPE: the macros `p-local-deref-{scalar,array,hash}` each need an init form,
the way `p-local-hash-elem-init` differs from `p-local-hash-elem` -- evaluated
BEFORE the slot is replaced (the stale-read rule `local($a[2]) = $a[2]`
established), and in LIST context for the array/hash sigils.  #564's
`p-local-glob-dynamic` is the worked example of the same addition on the glob
sigil, including the `if`/`unless` modifier slot (`t` = unconditional), which
this branch currently refuses with a loud drop.

BAR: the three sigils with and without an RHS, the symbolic and the
hard-reference spellings (localizing through a HARD ref dies in perl -- "Can't
localize through a reference" -- and the runtime macros already decide that at
run time), the statement-modifier forms, and the stale-read case
(`local ${$n} = ${$n} . "x"`).  corpus-diff; rows beside the #564 rows.
subject: `local ${EXPR} = RHS` DROPS THE ASSIGNMENT SILENTLY: the deref branch of _process_local_declaration localizes and then never emits the RHS
